reviewed_by: Codex focused Butler phase 1 capability gateway, parent-only child control, identity, settings, and iPhone layout review
reason: Butler uses a four-tool Core capability gateway shared by provider and harness turns; search, paging, and describe reveal selected-project actions on demand. Python coverage exercises project scoping, revision and schema validation, read/change separation, chat fork/delete/retry, main and child distinctions, parent-only messaging, native harness subagent and goal visibility, chat/goal/mission/approval controls, and the advertised catalog. Frontend coverage exercises the Nebula logo launcher, Butler identity, own settings, Voice labels, project-bound action receipts, and the recent-chat navigation guard when a work link opens another view. Selected real-Core LAN browser journeys cover small-context direct requests, discovery-driven mission creation, settings persistence, Core settings/help/navigation, and the centered phone assistant shell across desktop/mobile Chromium and WebKit. The LAN pairing fixture now waits for its committed redirect and mounted shell before navigating to project work. The README gains a compact vector architecture diagram. Final checks also cover settings-failure diagnostics and formatting/type-check corrections required by the selected CI lane.
exclusions: No native iOS or Rust source changed, so native tests are excluded. Browser and notes control remain deferred by the user. Generic provider, harness, streaming, unrelated pages and full suites are excluded. The harness integration selection is one exact test from its large shared file; the Settings runtime integration selection is one exact test. A physical iPhone check remains a separate acceptance gate; native harness task controls still need a live configured harness journey.
